The game is difficult, enemies are strong, and there's no meta-progression—each run starts anew and you're just relying on luck with the drops. Who cares if there are so many playable characters when it all feels the same anyway. I just can't get past it. Ugly graphics. 📝 Review
Brotato is like a bullet-hell salad with a side of rogue-lite chaos — messy, fast-paced, and oddly addictive. The gameplay loop hooks you quick and doesn’t let go, mixing frantic shooting with frantic dodging in a surprisingly satisfying way. The achievement list is a beast, but as a completionist, checking off all 176 was a rewarding marathon rather than a sprint.

It’s not the prettiest or deepest game out there, but it’s got personality, challenge, and that rare "just one more run" feeling that keeps you coming back. If you like your action loud and your progress relentless, Brotato delivers.

👍 Recommendation
Yes, I recommend it.

Brotato is an easy to get into game that hides a lot of complexity behind it.
It's an action rogue lite / bullet heaven where your main task is moving your character (like Vampire Survivors) and picking up upgrades between waves of enemies.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3374585825
It starts pretty easy, at the lowest difficulty, and there are easy ways to "break" the game thanks to item synergies.
But the more you play, the more characters you unlock: each one comes with a variation on stats / abilities.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3374585646
This means the strategy you used last time won't work now and you have to find a new one.
You don't get permanent upgrades after every run, but you get knowledge to do better the next time.
After a successful run, you unlock the next difficulty, which means bulkier enemies and more spawns.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3374585750
It feels pretty balanced, there are obviously overall better characters/builds but all the ones I personally tried were viable.
It's cheap and offers way more than its price tag, definetely worth a try!

I’ve put over 200 hours into Brotato, and it’s still one of my go-to games when I want something fast, challenging, and incredibly satisfying. The gameplay loop is perfect, every run feels different, and the mix of weapons, characters, and upgrades keeps things endlessly fresh.

The balance between chaos and strategy is spot on: you can jump in for a quick 10minute session or lose hours experimenting with new builds. The variety of characters and playstyles really lets you find your own groove, and the devs have done a great job keeping things polished and engaging.

Even after hundreds of hours, I’m still discovering fun synergies and new ways to push my limits. Brotato nails that “just one more run” feeling better than almost any roguelite out there.

What you see in the videos is what you're getting. One very bland square map with no obstructions or dangers to avoid, mass using 1-2 of the same type of weapon (your only build diversity) depending on the character. This repetition is more evident with time played. This has made beating every available character (your only progression) or pushing the high difficulties so boring/exhausting.

Till then, you don't even need to get that in-depth with synergies and number crunching as the reviews are making it appear. So long as you're generally buying the same important stats you can make a build work till the later danger levels (mostly RNG dependent). Don't get me wrong, its a good game but it's just, "good." Not what I would call overwhelmingly good as the rating would have you believe. With how popular this genre has now become, it's better to find one that has more variety/flavor in it.

I didn't quite have the magnetic, addictive pull to this that I had to its close cousin in Vampire Survivors, but it is certainly a tight, entertaining experience. While not as purely imaginative, I enjoy Brotato's bold-lined, cutesy art style far more than the pixel-throwback style of Vampire Survivors, which does a lot to carry it. The music is also superior, although Brotato seems to suffer from a lack of variety on that front.

There's enough here to unlock and enough different play styles to keep one engaged. This is a perfect Steam Deck game for me; it runs superbly well and is a great pick-up and put-down title when you have a few minutes to kill, or simply want to turn your brain off for a while after a hectic, stressful day.

Recommended to folks who enjoy roguelites or bullet heaven. Solid game.

Brotato is a surprisingly addictive top-down arena shooter roguelike that takes an absurd premise and turns it into pure, unadulterated fun. You play as a potato armed to the teeth with a wild array of weapons, battling endless waves of quirky enemies in chaotic, fast-paced combat. The graphics are simple yet charming—a colorful, cartoonish aesthetic that perfectly complements the game’s frenetic energy.

Gameplay is relentlessly engaging. Each run forces you to adapt as you dodge bullets, collect power-ups, and experiment with countless weapon combinations and modifiers. Every playthrough feels fresh, thanks to the diverse arsenal and randomized upgrades, even if the grind for unlocking new gear can sometimes catch you off guard. The challenge ramps up quickly, delivering just the right amount of tension without feeling unfair.

The audio matches the overall vibe—quirky, energetic, and satisfying, enhancing every frantic moment on screen. While Brotato might not boast AAA polish, its delightful blend of humor, challenge, and creative design makes it a standout entry in the roguelike genre.

9/10 — A spud-tacular, adrenaline-fueled experience that leaves you craving more.

I get the appeal, but this is not for me. For context, I was absolutely hooked on '20 Minutes Till Dawn' - another Bullet Heaven - but this game doesn't have the charm that game has.

Collecting these items, walking around aimlessly... There's no juice to it, no aspiration of creating a new build, no personality to attach myself. And granted, it's not like 20MTD is a Hugo-award winning piece of literature - but just the artstyle alone is something for my imagination to envision a quest against evil. I guess I just don't get what Brotato is aiming at - is it humor? A tongue-in-cheek vibe? Nothing here astounded me, unfortunately.
